prompts.prompt: What is the mass of NASA’s Curiosity rover itself, in kilograms?
prompts.scope: The mass of the rover itself as reported by NASA — not the launch mass with the cruise stage and descent hardware.

hint.text: Curiosity is about the size of a small SUV, but much of that volume is empty space and instrument decks.

image.alt: Illustration of the Curiosity rover beside three people for scale; the rover reaches roughly shoulder height. (Fixture placeholder artwork.)
image.rights: Original placeholder illustration for demonstration only

source.title: NASA Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) mission page

reveal.explanation: NASA lists the Curiosity rover’s own mass as 899 kg — about 15 adult humans, or roughly the mass of a grand piano plus its mover.
reveal.sourceTitle: NASA Mars Science Laboratory mission page
reveal.comparison: That is about the mass of a small car with nobody in it.

prompts.prompt: Roughly how many loaves of sandwich bread could you make from the wheat grown on one acre, using the fixture yield and a 450 g flour recipe? (The fixture uses 3,000 kg of wheat per acre, 0.75 kg of flour recovered per kg of wheat, and 0.45 kg of flour per loaf.)
prompts.scope: Demonstration fixture with declared assumptions: 3,000 kg wheat per acre, 75% flour extraction, 450 g flour per baked loaf. A live version would source crop, country and harvest year.

image.alt: Illustration of a standard 450 g sliced sandwich loaf beside a measuring cup of flour. (Fixture placeholder artwork.)
image.rights: Original placeholder illustration for demonstration only

inputs.name: wheatYield
inputs.assumption: Representative fixture yield for one acre of wheat (a live puzzle would source crop, country and year).

source.title: Fixture recipe: 450 g flour sandwich loaf

steps: One acre yields 3,000 kg of wheat (declared fixture assumption).
Milling recovers 75% as flour: 3,000 × 0.75 = 2,250 kg of flour.
Each loaf takes 0.45 kg of flour: 2,250 ÷ 0.45 = 5,000 loaves. Worked estimate: 5,000 loaves.

reveal.explanation: Wheat → flour → loaves: 3,000 kg × 0.75 ÷ 0.45 = 5,000 loaves per acre under the declared assumptions.
reveal.comparison: One acre (about the size of half a football pitch) could keep a small bakery in sandwich bread for a week.

prompts.prompt: How many individual steps would a representative runner take to finish a marathon? The official race distance is 42.195 km. The fixture assumes a 1.2 m step length.
prompts.scope: Representative runner model: 42.195 km at a 1.2 m step length (a typical easy-pace stride). A live puzzle would define the runner model in the scope.

hint.text: At an easy pace most runners take roughly 160–170 steps per minute — you can also work from stride length.

inputs.name: stepLength
inputs.assumption: Representative easy-pace stride length (declared in the prompt).

steps: Convert the official distance: 42.195 km = 42,195 m.
Divide by the assumed step length: 42,195 ÷ 1.2 = 35,162.5 steps.
Round to an editorially meaningful benchmark. Worked estimate: 35,000 steps.

reveal.explanation: 42,195 m ÷ 1.2 m per step ≈ 35,162.5, published as a representative benchmark of 35,000 steps.

prompts.prompt: How many sheets of standard office paper, stacked flat, would reach the top of the Eiffel Tower, including its antenna? The fixture uses a tower height of 330 m and a ream of 500 sheets about 5 cm thick.
prompts.scope: Declared fixture paper specification: 0.05 m per 500-sheet ream (0.1 mm per sheet). Tower height 330 m including antennas.

figure.scope: Thickness of the fixture’s standard office ream

source.title: Eiffel Tower official site (height with antennas)

steps: One ream is 0.05 m for 500 sheets, so one sheet is 0.05 ÷ 500 = 0.0001 m (0.1 mm).
Divide the tower height by the sheet thickness: 330 ÷ 0.0001.

reveal.explanation: A sheet of office paper is about 0.1 mm thick, so 330 m ÷ 0.0001 m = 3,300,000 sheets.

prompts.prompt: Name a feature film whose original theatrical runtime is closest to 150 minutes.
prompts.scope: Starter dataset: the fixture collection of ten films with original theatrical runtimes. Spell the title as closely as you can; suggestions appear as you type.

reveal.explanation: Your film’s runtime is compared against the target; the dataset’s closest eligible entries are shown.
